# ADS 506 Module 1 Assignment

This assignment is due on Day 7 of the learning week. The assignment for this module consists of code, outputs and short prose responses. Use R with [tidyverts](tidyverts.org) (`fpp3`) Complete the assignment in a [Quarto Document](quarto.org). Your submission should show all code executed and must not exceed 6 pages.

## 1) Shipments of Household Appliance:

The file ApplianceShipments.xls contains the series of quarterly shipments (in millions of USD) of U.S. household appliances between 1985-1989.

### a) Read the data into a `tsibble` and replace this plot with one that is created from code. Be sure to reproduce the plot exactly as it appears.

```{r ex1-a}
# Read data into a tsibble
shipments <- read_excel("../data/ApplianceShipments.xlsx") |>
    mutate(Quarter = yearquarter(Quarter)) |> 
    select(Quarter, Shipments) |> 
    as_tsibble(index = Quarter)

# Plot shipments
shipments |> autoplot(Shipments) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Appliance Shipments")

```

### b) Which of the four components (level, trend, seasonality, noise) seem to be present in this series? Show a plot to that supports your conclusions.

Based on the output below:

- Level is present, the shipments data exists between approximately 4,000 and 4,800 shipments per quarter.
- Trend is present, there is general upward trend over time.
- Seasonality is present, there is a consistent Q2 peak and a Q4 trough. Q3 is generally higher than Q1 as well.
- There is noise present in the time series as well, most noticeably in Q3 and Q4 1986, but noise is present throughout the time series.

```{r ex1-b}
# Create components plot
shipments |> model(stl = STL(Shipments)) |>
  components() |>
  autoplot()
```

### b) What is time interval for this series.

Interval: \[30M\], meaning there is a data point every 30 minutes.

### c) Use the `gafa_stock` dataset from `fpp3` to reproduce/replace the following plot

```{r ex2-c}
# Create gafa_stock plot
gafa_stock |> autoplot(Close) +
  facet_grid(vars(Symbol), scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Date")
```

### d) Plot The `us_total` from `USgas` package

- Install the `USgas` package. **IMPORTANT:** Comment or omit any code you use to do this, so the package is only installed once.
- Create a `tsibble` from `us_total` with `year` as the `index` and `state` as the `key`.
- Plot the annual natural gas consumption by state for the New England area (comprising the states of Maine, Vermont, New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Connecticut and Rhode Island). Ensure the y-axis is scaled and labeled appropriately with correct units. The objective of the plot is for the reader to compare consumption by state and estimate values over time.

```{r ex2-d}
# Create the tsibble
us_gas <- us_total |> as_tsibble(key = state, index = year)

# Ensure y-axis is not in scientific notation
options(scipen = 999)

# Create New England Subset
new_england <- c("Maine", "Vermont", "New Hampshire",
                 "Massachusetts", "Connecticut", "Rhode Island")

# Plot NE annual natural gas consumption, scaling the y-axis
us_gas |> filter(state %in% new_england) |>
  autoplot(y/1e6) + 
  labs(y = "Natural Gas Consumption (Million Cubic Feet)",
       title = "New England Natural Gas Consumption")
```
